records.literal_gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:

en.L: And the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:
en.B: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

decisions.choice: the parable of the vine: a short oracle in which the vine stands for Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The chapter is a parable (compare 17:2), built as a series of questions about vine wood (15:2-5), followed by its application to Jerusalem (15:6-8). It is set as prose, like the oracles around it, though its questions have the balance of verse.

source.text: בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם מַה־יִּֽהְיֶ֥ה עֵץ־הַגֶּ֖פֶן מִכָּל־עֵ֑ץ הַזְּמוֹרָ֕ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיָ֖ה בַּעֲצֵ֥י הַיָּֽעַר׃

records.literal_gloss: Son of man, what is [the] wood of the vine more than any wood, the branch that is among [the] trees of the forest?

en.L: Son of man, how is the wood of the vine more than any [other] wood, the vine branch that is among the trees of the forest?
en.B: Son of man, how is the wood of the vine any better than other wood, than a branch among the trees of the forest?
en.R: Son of man, is the wood of a grapevine any better than the wood of the trees in the forest?

decisions.choice: the vine: a picture of Israel, here turned against it
decisions.reason: Israel is often pictured as the LORD's vine or vineyard (Psalm 80:9-17; Isaiah 5:1-7; Jeremiah 2:21; Hosea 10:1), and Ezekiel returns to the picture in 17:5-10 and 19:10-14 (compare John 15:1-6). A vine is valued for its fruit; its wood is weak and crooked. The parable asks only about the wood, and so leaves Israel no ground for pride.

decisions.choice: the branch among the trees of the forest: the vine, growing wild among the forest trees, or the other trees' wood
alternatives: how is the vine better than any branch found among the forest trees?
decisions.reason: The phrase may describe the vine itself, a wild vine among the trees, or the wood it is compared with. Either way the question expects the answer that vine wood is no better than any other, and in fact worse (15:3).
Readable makes clear that the plant is a grapevine.

source.text: הֲיֻקַּ֤ח מִמֶּ֨נּוּ֙ עֵ֔ץ לַעֲשׂ֖וֹת לִמְלָאכָ֑ה אִם־יִקְח֤וּ מִמֶּ֨נּוּ֙ יָתֵ֔ד לִתְל֥וֹת עָלָ֖יו כָּל־כֶּֽלִי׃

records.literal_gloss: [Is] taken from it wood to make into work? Or do they take from it a peg to hang on it any vessel?

en.L: Is wood taken from it to make [it into any] work? Or do they take a peg from it to hang any vessel on?
en.B: Can wood be taken from it to make anything useful? Can anyone make a peg from it to hang things on?
en.R: Can its wood be used to make anything? Can anyone even make a peg from it to hang a pot on?

decisions.choice: a peg to hang a vessel on: the simplest use of wood, and even that is impossible
decisions.reason: Pegs were driven into walls to hang pots and tools (compare Isaiah 22:23-25). Vine wood is too soft and crooked even for that.

source.text: הִנֵּ֥ה לָאֵ֖שׁ נִתַּ֣ן לְאָכְלָ֑ה אֵת֩ שְׁנֵ֨י קְצוֹתָ֜יו אָכְלָ֤ה הָאֵשׁ֙ וְתוֹכ֣וֹ נָחָ֔ר הֲיִצְלַ֖ח לִמְלָאכָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Behold, to the fire it is given for fuel; its two ends the fire has consumed, and its middle is charred; is it useful for work?

en.L: Look, it is given to the fire for fuel; the fire has consumed both its ends, and its middle is charred. Is it useful for [any] work?
en.B: No, it is thrown into the fire as fuel. When the fire has burned up both ends and the middle is charred, is it good for anything?
en.R: No, it is only good for burning. When fire has burned up both ends and blackened the middle, can it be used for anything?

decisions.choice: both ends burned and the middle charred: a nation already partly destroyed
alternatives: a detail of the picture with no separate meaning
decisions.reason: A stick in the fire burns from both ends toward the middle. Many readers see in the ends the losses already suffered, such as the fall of the northern kingdom in 722 BC and the exile of 597 BC, and in the charred middle the Jerusalem that remains. The text gives only the picture.

source.text: הִנֵּה֙ בִּֽהְיוֹת֣וֹ תָמִ֔ים לֹ֥א יֵֽעָשֶׂ֖ה לִמְלָאכָ֑ה אַ֣ף כִּי־אֵ֤שׁ אֲכָלַ֨תְהוּ֙ וַיֵּחָ֔ר וְנַעֲשָׂ֥ה ע֖וֹד לִמְלָאכָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Behold, when it is whole, not it is made into work; how much less when fire has consumed it and it is charred, will it yet be made into work?

en.L: Look, while it was whole, it could not be made into [any] work; how much less, when fire has consumed it and it is charred, can it still be made into [any] work!
en.B: Even when it was whole, it could not be made into anything useful. How much less can it be made into anything useful once the fire has burned it and it is charred!
en.R: Even when it was whole, no one could make anything from it. Now that the fire has burned it and blackened it, it is even more useless!

decisions.choice: how much less: if it was useless whole, it is worse than useless burned
decisions.reason: The argument moves from the lesser to the greater, as in 14:21.

source.text: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר עֵץ־הַגֶּ֨פֶן֙ בְּעֵ֣ץ הַיַּ֔עַר אֲשֶׁר־נְתַתִּ֥יו לָאֵ֖שׁ לְאָכְלָ֑ה כֵּ֣ן נָתַ֔תִּי אֶת־יֹשְׁבֵ֖י יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: As [the] wood of the vine among [the] trees of the forest, which I have given to the fire for fuel, so I give up [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem.

en.L: Therefore thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: As the wood of the vine [is] among the trees of the forest, which I have handed over to the fire as food, so I have handed over the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
en.B: Therefore the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: As with the vine's wood among the forest trees, which I have handed over to the fire to burn, so I will hand over the people who live in Jerusalem.
en.R: So this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I have given the wood of the grapevine to the fire to burn, just like the wood of the trees in the forest. In the same way I will give up the people of Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: so I give up the inhabitants of Jerusalem: the parable applied
decisions.reason: The fire's "food" is its fuel. The verb is a past form that speaks of the judgment as already decided. Jerusalem, like vine wood, has no worth apart from the fruit it should have borne. It will be given to the fire, as the city was burned in 586 BC (2 Kings 25:9).

source.text: וְנָתַתִּ֤י אֶת־פָּנַי֙ בָּהֶ֔ם מֵהָאֵ֣שׁ יָצָ֔אוּ וְהָאֵ֖שׁ תֹּֽאכְלֵ֑ם וִֽידַעְתֶּם֙ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה בְּשׂוּמִ֥י אֶת־פָּנַ֖י בָּהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will set my face against them; from the fire they have come out, and the fire will consume them; and you will know that I [am] Yahweh, when I set my face against them.

en.L: And I will set {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face against them; out of the fire they have come, yet the fire will consume them; and you will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I have set {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face against them.
en.B: I will set {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face against them. They have come out of the fire, but the fire will still burn them up. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I turn {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face against them.
en.R: I will turn against them. They have escaped from one fire, but another fire will burn them up. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I turn against them.

decisions.choice: out of the fire they have come, yet the fire will consume them: they survived one disaster, but not the next
decisions.reason: The people of Jerusalem had come through the siege and deportation of 597 BC. Like a half-burned stick pulled from the fire (compare Amos 4:11), they will not escape the fire that is coming.

decisions.choice: set my face against them: turn against them in judgment (compare 14:8)
decisions.reason: The LORD's face, which should mean his favor (Numbers 6:25-26), is turned against them, as in 14:8 and Leviticus 20:3-6.

decisions.choice: you will know that I am the LORD (see 6:7)

alternatives: I will set my face against them
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means (m2).

source.text: וְנָתַתִּ֥י אֶת־הָאָ֖רֶץ שְׁמָמָ֑ה יַ֚עַן מָ֣עֲלוּ מַ֔עַל נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And I will make the land a desolation, because they have acted faithlessly, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.

en.L: And I will make the land a desolation, because they have acted faithlessly, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: I will make the land a desolation because they have been unfaithful, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: I will make the land empty and ruined because the people have been unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: acted faithlessly: broken faith with the LORD (see 14:13)
decisions.reason: The same words describe the land's sin in 14:13. The parable of the vine ends where that oracle began.
Readable says to whom they were unfaithful.
